historical_events.description: Jamaica discovered by Columbus on his third voyage, called it St. Jago
Jamaica capitulated to British force under Admirals Penn and Venables after 161 years of Spanish possession
Slavery abolished in Jamaica, £1,161,927 granted as compensation to slaveowners
Hong Kong, then a desolate island sparsely inhabited by fishermen, first ceded to Great Britain
Charter for Hong Kong government issued
Kow-loon peninsula (28 square miles) ceded to Great Britain by Treaty entered into by Lord Elgin
Sovereignty of Fiji ceded to Her Majesty by Thakombau, Maafu, and other principal chiefs in deed of cession
Epidemic of measles greatly reduced native population
Gibraltar captured by British forces under Sir George Rooke
Gibraltar ceded to Great Britain by Treaty of Utrecht
Gibraltar successfully defended by Gen. Eliot (afterwards Lord Heathfield) during great siege
Falkland Islands discovered by Davis, visited by Hawkins in 1594
Falkland Islands taken possession of by British Government for protection of Whale Fishery
historical_events.prior_history: Republic of Buenos Ayres settlement destroyed by Americans in 1831

historical_events.description: During Roman occupation, shipwreck of Paul took place (Acts xxviii)

historical_events.event: Malta granted to Knights of St. John
historical_events.description: Malta granted by Roman Emperor Charles V to Order of Knights of St. John, held for more than two centuries
Grand Master Hompesch capitulated to Napoleon Bonaparte, who dispersed the Order
Malta finally annexed to British Crown by Treaty of Paris
Peninsula of Sierra Leone ceded to Great Britain by native chiefs
Charter granted to Sierra Leone Company for establishing settlement for freed negro slaves
Governor Sir Charles Macarthy killed at Essamkow leading army against Ashantis
War against Ashanti kingdom, culminating in British forces entering Coomassie on 4 February 1874
Provinces of Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick, and Nova Scotia formed into one Dominion by Imperial Act 30 Vic., c. 3
Canadian Pacific Railway connecting Atlantic with Pacific Ocean completed, opened for general traffic Montreal to Vancouver
War between British forces and Zulu kingdom under Cetywayo, including battles of Isandlwana, Rorke's Drift, and Ulundi

key_battles.name: Rorke's Drift
key_battles.result: British defence, one company 24th Regiment held post

key_battles.name: Ulundi
key_battles.result: British victory, Zulu military power broken

historical_events.description: Cetywayo re-installed by Sir Theophilus Shepstone in presence of 5,000 Zulus, after visiting England
Cetywayo died while living in the Reserve under care of Resident
Zululand formally declared British territory with general assent of Zulus
Trinidad first discovered by Columbus on his third voyage, taken possession of for Crown of Spain
Trinidad surrendered to British forces, articles of capitulation signed
Trinidad finally ceded to Crown of Great Britain by Treaty of Amiens
Island of Labuan, then uninhabited, ceded to Great Britain by Sultan of Borneo
Heligoland surrendered to British arms
Heligoland formally ceded to Great Britain by Denmark in Treaty of Kiel
